articles.paper: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
articles.authors: Jaemyung Yu · Byeongho Heo · Sangdoo Yun · Dongyoon Han
articles.title: Recovering second moments with input-side rotation

blocks.text: SOAP (2024) maintains rotations on both sides of the gradient matrix and runs Adam in the rotated basis. FOAM keeps the input eigenvectors Q and uses row and column statistics in the spirit of Adafactor (2018). Let G be the m×n gradient matrix, with input and output second-moment factors R and L. [1]

blocks.label: Lemma 1; assumes K-FAC separability and column-major vectorization
Eq. (6); bias-corrected EMAs of row and column means, with reconstructed mass fixed at tr(R)

blocks.text: Experiments tune each optimizer at 124M, 350M, and 760M. The table uses the 760M model, 15.49B FineWeb tokens, and 8×H100. Final losses are three-seed means ± standard deviations. Time to target uses the same validation-loss threshold of 2.847 in every row. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Under the factorization, the population second moment sums to tr(R)tr(L). Eq. (6) therefore recovers the rank-one shape in the population; the written normalization requires tr(L)=1 for the absolute scale. Measured times depend on the training parallelization. [1]

articles.paper: Lara Mini Base: Language Diversity as a Resource, Not a Trade-off
articles.title: Replacing multilingual data from a fixed checkpoint

blocks.text: Translated’s MoE base has 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters and trains on roughly 6T tokens. From a 5.4T checkpoint, the authors run two 100B-token anneals, replacing multilingual data with English in one branch. Writing scores as a function of mixture weights makes the direction of substitution explicit. [2]

blocks.label: Notation for these notes; coordinates are English, other languages, and code/math/SFT-like data; j indexes benchmark groups

blocks.text: Separate single-run, 100B-token ablations compare optimizers around 0.5B active parameters. Reading the curves at matched training loss, the authors report that AdamW needs 1.5–1.9 times as many tokens as Muon. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The mixture comparison covers one late checkpoint and one substitution direction. Full-run mixture effects, the separate contributions of routing and data selection, and end-to-end time at matched quality remain unresolved. [2]

title: One-sided preconditioning and multilingual data mixtures
subtitle: FOAM · Lara Mini Base · Constitutional AI
intro: FOAM approximates the rotated second moment with two vectors and benchmarks against Muon at three scales. Lara Mini Base starts from a common checkpoint to measure the effect of substituting English for multilingual data over the final 100B-token branches. The classic unpacks principle sampling and soft labels in Constitutional AI.

classic.title: Turning written principles into preference supervision
classic.paper: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
classic.authors: Yuntao Bai · Saurav Kadavath · Sandipan Kundu · Amanda Askell · et al.
classic.evidence: Read §3–4; equations formalize the reported pipeline
classic.question: If principles systematically disagree about a class of responses, how would you design stratified sampling and a holdout set to distinguish judge miscalibration from genuine disagreement among principles?

blocks.text: The 2022 helpful-and-harmless RLHF work trains a preference model from human comparisons. Constitutional AI splits harmlessness supervision into two decisions: have a model revise answers using written principles, then have an independent feedback model compare responses under a principle. Helpfulness labels still come from humans. [7,9]

blocks.text: In the human Elo comparisons in §4.3, RL-CAI scored higher on harmlessness than the RLHF and SL-CAI systems in the paper. Overconfidence in chain-of-thought feedback led the authors to clamp those soft targets to [0.4, 0.6]. Longer RL runs still produced boilerplate or overly stern responses. Elo measures relative preferences; transfer to other populations and prompt distributions requires evaluation. [7]
